summary: IDS feed s139_double is degraded: 3.34 Gbps microbursts overwhelm 1 Gbps IDS port (334% overload) causing 6.5% TCP packet drops - IDS receives incomplete traffic and misses detections.

findings.root_cause: Peak traffic hits 3.34 Gbps in 1ms bursts vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (334% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals) - port buffers overflow and tail-drop. IDS requires both directions and full payload, so any burst over 1G causes loss.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops packets under load, cannot reassemble TCP streams or match signatures during bursts, creating blind spots and allowing exploits to evade detection

recommended_fix.why: Distribute microbursts across multiple 1G tool ports (or upgrade to 10G) with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization <80% and preserve both directions per flow for IDS state tracking

findings.root_cause: 122 of 1880 TCP packets (6.5% vs 1% threshold) show missing data/gaps - broker/SPAN buffers dropping packets when 3.3 Gbps bursts exceed 1G tool port. Correlated directly with tool_overload bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees truncated flows and incomplete payload, fails to detect multi-packet attacks, suffers TCP reassembly failures and false negatives; 6.5% loss severely degrades detection coverage

recommended_fix.why: Load balancing is required instead of slicing/filtering because IDS needs_full_payload=true - slicing would break payload inspection, load balancing preserves full flows while eliminating congestion drops
